newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel holds despite high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel holds despite high stocks.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices held steady despite brimming stocks and weak demand, traders said on Thursday.
Late Asian trading day, a European major sold a June 27-July 1 cargo to a local trader at $23.35 a barrel.
Traders said the local trader had emerged in an attempt to hold the market at their current levels.
They said fundamentals were still weak and levels are unlikely to sustain current prices unless China emerged to soak up the surplus supplies.
At least four western traders have fixed arbitrage cargoes from the west to the east. These cargoes were expected to arrive by mid July, traders said.
They said high stocks have caused some majors to offer cash supplies for July loading at a 10-20 cents discount to Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.
Brimming stocks and the lack of outlets have also caused Singapore Petroleum Co's (SPC) to store supplies outside its refinery complex.
"The tank top situation has caused the refinery to move cargoes cross harbour to store at available storage capacities at Caltex and SPC," said one trader.

The high stock level was reflected in data released by the Singapore's Trade Development Board which showed that middle distillate stocks have risen by 993,000 barrels to 11.236 million barrels for the week ending June 11.
The stocks are at their highest since at least Janaury 1994.

But refineries in Singapore were unwilling to cut runs despite high inventories, citing healthy margins. They said refiners were able to sustained positive margins as crude prices have fallen by a larger extent compared to products.
Demand however remained weak. Pockets of enquries were heard from China but buyers were quoting at below $175 while offers at above $176 per tonne c+f South China.
Traders in Hong Kong said a Chinese joint venture refinery was also offering supplies, Offer were heard at a high of $175 per tonne free-on-board Dalian.
The refiner said it is not pushed to offer the supplies given current weak market conditions.
